title: Choose the visual world
question: Does the Living Index fit the personal-site use case, or should we re-roll with another steer?

options.label: Living Index
options.lineage: artist monographs, independent magazines, and authored personal homepages
options.thesis: An immediately legible personal index whose editorial rhythm is transformed by artwork at consequential moments.
options.viewport: Mathieu's name, concise orientation, and familiar navigation are immediately visible; one asymmetrical artwork and a dense but calm index introduce Work and Writing without disguising the page as another object.
options.risk: Without decisive image scale, typographic character, and transitions, it could collapse into a merely tasteful portfolio or blog.
options.case: It identifies the subject and purpose immediately while reserving the expressive ceiling for composition, imagery, pacing, and motion.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A restrained introduction followed by selected work, recent writing, reading, and contact in a familiar responsive grid.
canonCard.viewport: Mathieu's name and short introduction lead beside one artwork, followed immediately by selected work and recent writing.
canonCard.risk: Highly legible and credible, but the personal world and interactive ambition may not become memorable.
